title: Consensus Roadmap Log: onboarding stakeholder knowledge and structured decision ledger
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales, decisions about which customer-driven items get roadmap slots are fragmented across PMs, CSMs, and Sales. This leads to inconsistent trade-offs, repeated rework during exec reviews, and loss of institutional knowledge when account owners change.

Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable Consensus Roadmap Log (CRL) and an onboarding checklist for account stakeholders that: 1) captures the key signals and trade-offs for each top-account ask; 2) provides a single source of truth for historical decisions; and 3) surfaces recommended outcomes for PM prioritization cycles.

Scope: Pilot for top-30 accounts and high-severity escalations over two cycles (2025-W05 and 2025-W09). Deliverables: CRL template (Confluence), an intake checklist for CSMs, a one-click export for exec-review slide, and a small simulator for slot reallocation (spreadsheet).

Out of scope: Replacing current intake forms entirely, changing pricing or contractual obligations. This is governance + artifact standardization to reduce friction and decision churn.
acceptance_criteria: A CRL Confluence template exists that records: ask summary, customer metrics (ARR, growth), user impact, requested timeline, dependencies, proposed mitigation plan, and final decision rationale.
Onboarding checklist published and distributed to CSMs; checklist used in at least 12 pilot intake artifacts.
An exec-review slide export button (CSV -> templated slide) is validated and used in the Cycle-01 review meeting.
A simple slot-reallocation simulator (Google Sheet) that models 3 roadmap slots, prioritization scores, and shows NPV-like impact for changes.
At least two historical decision logs are backfilled and reviewed with stakeholders to validate fidelity and learnings capture.
notes: Design principle: keep CRL < 600 words per ask; decision rationale must be explicit (why this over other asks).
Trade-off fields: resource cost estimate (FTE weeks), risk to existing SLOs, legal/compliance flags, potential revenue retention/growth estimate, customer advocacy/market signal.
Scoring rubric draft: combination of ARR-weighted signal (0-40), product-strategic-fit (0-30), implementation complexity (0-15 reversed), and churn risk (0-15). Final score normalized to 100.
Pilot cadence: weekly intake QC with CSM leads (Thursdays 11-11:30am PT), biweekly PM prioritization sync (Mondays 9am PT).
Dependencies: minor engineering support for the CSV export (one backend endpoint), Confluence template creation, and CSM adoption training.
